title: Founding Gotham Capital with a special-situations mandate
statement: Greenblatt started Gotham Capital with about $7 million to specialize in spinoffs, restructurings, rights offerings, mergers and other special situations — inefficiencies too small or complicated for large institutions.
outcome: Gotham compounded at roughly 50% annually in its first decade, among the best records ever reported, before Greenblatt returned outside capital in 1995 to manage his own money.

title: Writing 'You Can Be a Stock Market Genius'
statement: Greenblatt wrote the first accessible treatment of special-situations investing, laying out the mechanics of spinoffs, merger securities and recapitalizations for the ordinary investor.
outcome: The book remains the standard reference for event-driven investing and launched a generation of hedge fund careers.

title: Creating the Magic Formula and publishing it free
statement: Greenblatt systematized value plus quality — ranking stocks by cheapness (earnings yield) and return on capital — into a mechanical strategy he published openly, with free screening tools, in 'The Little Book That Beats the Market.'
outcome: The book sold over a million copies; independent studies found the formula's long-run backtest excess returns though with punishing drawdowns, illustrating Greenblatt's own caveat that simple does not mean easy.

title: Value Investors Club — founding the vetted online community
statement: Greenblatt created an online investment club whose membership, capped and competitively admitted, shares detailed investment write-ups subject to peer rating.
outcome: The club became a recognized training ground for value analysts and a rare example of durable, high-quality crowdsourced investment research.

title: Formula Investing / Gotham Funds — bringing the formula to institutions
statement: After the 2008 crisis, Greenblatt launched actively managed mutual funds applying systematic value-and-quality strategies at institutional scale.
outcome: The funds grew to several billion under management; performance was solid though below the backtests, an honest outcome Greenblatt himself used to teach the difference between in-sample and live results.

title: Columbia Business School teaching — the special-situations course
statement: Greenblatt taught the value and special-situations curriculum at Columbia, co-authoring the case-driven text 'Value Investing: From Graham to Buffett and Beyond.'
outcome: His course shaped numerous prominent value investors and kept the Graham tradition anchored in actionable, situation-specific analysis.
